desc: The joint interagency task force the Department stood up in August 2025, directed by Brig. Gen. Matt Ross, to handle unmanned aircraft incursions over US installations after two years in which no existing command could stop them. Its creation is the institutional concession that the 2023-2024 incursions were a real, persistent, unattributed operational problem rather than a public-misperception problem. The Department of Defense Inspector General's report DODIG-2026-045, dated 21 January 2026, evaluated ten installations that had experienced drone incursions and interviewed officials from 31 DoD components and four federal agencies, finding inconsistent policies and approval processes, unclear designation of 'covered' facilities under federal law leaving some installations without counter-drone authority, and approval requirements that delayed deployment of systems bases already possessed. Nine days later, on 30 January 2026, the Department issued guidance removing the 'fence-line' limitation on commanders' response authority, defining 'unauthorized surveillance' as an explicit threat, and granting 'totality of circumstances' discretion. Restricted-airspace sightings had risen 26 percent in 2025.
